sentences.text: SINGLE BENCH : HON'BLE JUSTICE NANDITA DUBEY  Writ Petition No.9828/2019  M/s
Rameshwaram Transport

Vs.
 State of Madhya Pradesh and others ________________________________
_ _ _  Shri Sankalp Kochar, learned counsel for the  petitioner.

Ms. Prashansa Bais, learned Panel Lawyer for the  respondent/State.
 Shri Shobhitaditya learned counsel for respondents  No.2 and 3.
 ORDER (09.11.2021)

The petitioner is aggrieved by the order dated 13.02.2019 (Anneuxre P-12), issued by the Managing Director, M.P. State Civil Supplies Corporation Limited (hereinafter referred to as 'the Corporation') blacklisting it for a period of 10 years for alleged irregularity pointed therein.

entities.text: M.P. State Civil Supplies Corporation Limited
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 2. The petitioner, entered into an agreement with respondent on 01.09.2015, for a duration till 30.06.2017, for transportation of grains to the lead societies under the Shahpura District Centre from godowns under 'Dwar Praday Yojana of year 2017'.

The petitioner was served with an order of termination-cum-blacklisting dated 14.06.2016, debarring it from participating in future bids for 10 years by invoking clause 40 of the terms and conditions of NIT.

It was suspected that the petitioner has used forged receipts and the grains were transported and black-marketed at other than destined sector.
3. Petitioner assailed the aforesaid order by way of W.P. No.12878/2016, on the ground that the order impugned was passed without affording opportunity of hearing, thereby violating the principles of natural justice and has caused a great prejudice to the petitioner preventing him from M/S Rameshwaram Transport vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 November, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57735395/
1 participating in similar tenders.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Taking note of the fact that the impugned order dated 14.06.2016 was a termination-cum-blacklisting order, the petition was directed to be entertained only on the issue as to blacklisting the petitioner, whereas, against the termination of contract, the petitioner was set at liberty to pursue the remedy of arbitration.
The writ petition was finally disposed of vide order 26.09.2016 and the order of blacklisting was quashed.
The matter was relegated to the competent authority to pass fresh orders on blacklisting after affording an opportunity of hearing to the petitioner.
It was further observed that, "this remand order will not create any right in the petitioner to claim fresh contract or the continuation of the existing contract.

The reasons being that, the allegation against the petitioner are serious enough for the respondent corporation to exercise its discretion till the petitioner is cleared of and exonerated of the allegation."
4. It is a matter of record that a Writ Appeal bearing No.764/2016 was thereafter preferred for expunging the said observation.

The same, however, came to be withdrawn on 03.10.2017 with liberty to challenge the subsequent order dated 21.11.2016 passed by the competent authority,
pursuant to order dated 26.09.2016.

5. In the meanwhile, on the same set of facts, the District Magistrate, Jabalpur also passed an order of detention dated 11.07.2016 against the transporter/owner/proprietor of the company, exercising the power under Section 8 of Prevention of Black-marketing and Maintenance of Supplies of Essential Commodities Act, 1980.

entities.text: Prevention of Black-marketing and Maintenance of Supplies of Essential Commodities Act, 1980
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
The order of detention was challenged by way of W.P.
No.19671/2016, which came to be dismissed on 08.05.2017.

It is a matter of record that after dismissal of the writ petition, an application for reconsideration was preferred before the Ministry of Home and Internal Affairs, whereupon a detailed report from the Collector/District Magistrate,
Jabalpur as well as from the District Manager of the Corporation was called for in regard to the illegalities committed.

entities.text: Ministry of Home and Internal Affairs
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The Statement of shop owners of concerned fair price shops were also got recorded by the authorities, who verified the fact that food grains were duly supplied to the different fair price shops.

In view of these subsequent evidence and reports, petitioner preferred a R.P.
No.1277/2017 for recalling the order dated 08.05.2017.
The review petition was allowed and the order of detention dated 11.07.2016 was quashed.

6. In the light of these subsequent documents/evidence and letters dated 08.09.2017 and 08.01.2018, forwarded by respondent No.3 to respondent No.2 to withdraw/cancel the order of blacklisting, the petitioner submitted a fresh representation before the authorities for reconsideration of his case, which unfortunately, remained pending.

The petitioner thereafter preferred W.P. No.25551/2018, which was disposed of on 12.12.2018 with a direction to the authority to decide the pending representation in the light of order passed in R.P. No.1277/2017 and in view of the official communication dated 08.01.2018.
In pursuant to the same, the respondent No.1 rejected the representation of the petitioner, which has led to filing of present petition.
7. Shri Sankalp Kochar, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submitted that the impugned order is arbitrary, illegal and contrary to the directions given by this Court in W.P. No. 25551/2018.

Referring to clause 40.2 of the NIT and the communication dated 08.09.2017 and 08.01.2018, it is urged that clause 40.2 envisages imposition of penalty of blacklisting under the recommendation of the District Manager and concerned Regional Manager of the Corporation, however, in the present M/S Rameshwaram Transport vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 November, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57735395/
2 case

entities.text: Rameshwaram Transport vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: the District Manager himself has recommended for withdrawal/cancellation of the order of blacklisting.

It is further submitted that the directions of this Court and also the subsequent report and the statements of the shop keepers, though brought to the notice of competent authority were deliberately ignored and overlooked and his representation was dismissed with malafide intent,
holding that the petitioner has failed to bring any new facts or evidence on record.
8.

It is argued on behalf of respondents No.2 and 3/Corporation that the concerned clause 26 of NIT clearly stated that only authorized vehicles will be used for transportation under the scheme, and any other vehicle could only be used for the purpose of transportation with the prior sanction/permission of Corporation or Collector.
Petitioner, however, without any such permission used the vehicles which were not authorized/ mentioned in the agreement.

He further contended that in the preliminary investigation, it was found that the food grains were never supplied to the fair price shop and the same were misappropriated for which the answering respondent has duly invoked clause 40.2 of the contract and imposing the penalty for blacklisting against the petitioner.

9. Heard the learned counsel for the parties at length and perused the record.
10.

The legal position on 'blacklisting' has been settled by a long list of the Supreme Courts' decision,
that the party against whom an order of blacklisting is passed should not only be given a fair opportunity of hearing but also the order itself be reasonable, fair and proportionate to the gravity of the offence.
Action of blacklisting is 'civil death' for the party/entity and needs to be tested on the principles of natural justice, fair play in action and on the doctrine of proportionality.

11. The effect of blacklisting has been high lighted by Supreme Court in the case of (2021) 2 SCC 551 UMC Technologies Private Limited Vs. Food Corporation of India and another, held thus :-
"14.

entities.text: (2021) 2 SCC 551 UMC Technologies Private Limited Vs. Food Corporation of India and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Specifically, in the context of blacklisting of a person or an entity by the state or a state corporation, the requirement of a valid, particularized and unambiguous show cause notice is particularly crucial due to the severe consequences of blacklisting and the stigmatization that accrues to the person/entity being blacklisted.
Here, it may be gainful to describe the concept of blacklisting and the graveness of the consequences occasioned by it.
Blacklisting has the effect of denying a person or an entity the privileged opportunity of entering into government contracts.

This privilege arises because it is the State who is the counterparty in government contracts and as such,
every eligible person is to be afforded an equal opportunity to participate in such contracts, without arbitrariness and discrimination.
Not only does blacklisting takes away this privilege, it also tarnishes the blacklisted person's reputation and brings the person's character into question.
Blacklisting also has long-lasting civil consequences for the future business prospects of the blacklisted person."

12. In Kulja Industries Limited Vs. Chief General Manager, Western Telecom Project Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited and others (2014) 14 SCC 731, while referring to the passage from the decision in Mahabir Auto Stores Vs. Indian Oil Corporation (1990) 3 SCC 752, the Supreme Court has held :-

sentences.text:
It is also well settled that even though the right of the writ petitioner is in the nature of a contractual right, the manner, the method and the motive behind the decision of the authority whether or not to enter into a contract is subject to judicial review on the touchstone of fairness, relevance, natural justice, non-discrimination,
equality and proportionality.

All these considerations that go to determine whether the action is sustainable in law have been sanctified by judicial pronouncements of this Court and are of seminal importance in a system that is committed to the rule of law.
We do not consider it necessary to burden this judgment by a copious reference to the decisions on the subject.

A reference to the following passage from the decision of this Court in M/s Mahabir Auto Stores & Ors. v. Indian Oil Corporation Ltd.,
(1990) 3 SCC 752 should, in our view, suffice:

entities.text:
M/s Mahabir Auto Stores & Ors. v. Indian Oil Corporation Ltd.,
(1990) 3 SCC 752
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "12. It is well settled that every action of the State or an instrumentality of the State in exercise of its executive power, must be informed by reason.

In appropriate cases,
actions uninformed by reason may be questioned as arbitrary in proceedings under Article 226 or Article 32 of the Con- situation.

Reliance in this connection may be placed on the observations of this Court in M/s Radha Krishna Agarwal & Ors. v.
State of Bihar & Ors., [1977] 3 SCC 457 .....

entities.text:
Radha Krishna Agarwal & Ors. v.
State of Bihar & Ors., [1977] 3 SCC 457
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In case any right conferred on the citizens which is sought to be interfered, such action is subject to Article 14 of the Constitution, and must be reasonable .....

It appears to us that rule of reason and rule against arbitrariness and discrimination, rules of fair play and natural justice are part of the rule of law applicable in situation or action by State instrumentality in dealing with citizens in a situation like the present one.

Even though the rights of the citizens are in the nature of contractual rights, the manner, the method and motive of a decision of entering or not entering into a contract, are subject to judicial review on the touchstone of relevance and reasonableness, fair play, natural justice, equality and non-discrimination in the type of the transactions and nature of the dealing as in the present case."
13. In Erusian Equipment and Chemicals Limited Vs. State of West Bengal (1975) 1 SCC 70, the Supreme Court has held:-
17.

entities.text: Erusian Equipment and Chemicals Limited Vs. State of West Bengal (1975) 1 SCC 70
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Government is a Government of laws and not of men.

It is true that neither the petitioner nor the respondent has any right to enter into a contract but they are entitled to equal treatment with others who offer tender or quotations for the purchase of the goods.

This privilege arises because it is the Government which is trading with the public and the democratic form of Government demands equality and absence of arbitrariness and discrimination in such transactions.
Hohfeld treats privileges as a form of liberty as opposed to a duty.
The activities of the Government have a public element and, therefore, there should be fairness and equality.
The State need not enter into any contract with any one but if it does so, it must do so fairly without discrimination and without unfair procedure.
Reputation is a part of a person's character and personality.
Blacklisting tarnishes one's reputation."

sentences.text: Applying the ratio of the aforesaid decisions to the facts of the present case, it is difficult to accept the arguments of learned counsel for the respondents.

Clause 40.2 of NIT authorises the Corporation to blacklist any transporter/contractor upto a period of 10 years, if he is found to have intentionally caused delay, misappropriation of food grains, adulteration or any other fraudulent action, and provides for termination of all existing contract/agreement of the transporter/contractor besides the forfeiture of the security amount of the said transporter/contractor alongwith the appropriate action for any outstanding recovery being taken by the Corporation.
16.

Blacklisting is thus an extreme recourse for disciplining such supplier/contractor, who have intentionally committed breach of conditions/regulations under the contract or committed acts of omission and commission or fraud including falsification of record, misrepresentation.

However,
the period of black listing would depend upon the nature of offence committed by the erring contractor/supplier.

17. In the instant case, while disposing of the W.P. No.25551/2018, this Court has directed the respondent authority to decide/consider the representation of petitioner dated 10.10.2018 in the light of order dated 23.03.2018 passed in R.P. No.1277/2017 and in view of the communication dated 08.01.2018.
However, the representation of the petitioner was dismissed vide order dated 13.02.2019.
According to the respondents, the petitioner has used unauthorized vehicle for transportation and the grains were not delivered at the designated Shahpura sector.

The order further mentioned that petitioner has not produced any new facts before the concerned authority and therefore, affirmed the order dated 21.11.2016.
18.

It is evident from the order dated 23.03.2018 passed in R.P. No.1277/2017 that the Ministry of Home Affairs summed the report from the Collector/District Magistrate, Jabalpur and also from the District Manager of the Corporation in regard to the illegalities committed by the petitioner,
wherein the statements of shop owners of concerned fair price shops were recorded by the authorities, who verified that food grains were duly supplied to them.
These documents/reports and statements were obtained by the petitioner under RTI and filed alongwith the review petition.

The Review Court after considering that these documents which notably were not denied by the respondent authorities, quashed the order of detention with liberty to the authority to pass appropriate orders after verification of the facts in the light of subsequent materials and evidence brought on record.

19. It is undisputed that after the order passed in R.P. No. 1277/2017, no fresh action for detention was taken against the petitioner rather the District Manager of the Corporation vide letters dated 08.09.2017, 08.01.2018 and subsequently on 08.03.2021, urged the Managing Directer of the M/S Rameshwaram Transport vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 November, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57735395/
5 Corporation, District Vigilance Officer, Collector Office and District Supply Officer, Jabalpur and recommended withdrawal/cancellation of the order of blacklisting of petitioner.

21. The Corporation is an instrumentality of State and expected to act and deal in a fair manner.
Its activities has a public element and therefore, there should be fairness and equality.

In the present case, no case of misappropriation or fraud is made out nor any loss has been caused to the Corporation, under the circumstances, the order of recovery and blacklisting cannot be sustained.

22. opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The legal position on 'blacklisting' has been settled by a long list of the Supreme Courts' decision,
that the party against whom an order of blacklisting is passed should not only be given a fair opportunity of hearing but also the order itself be reasonable, fair and proportionate to the gravity of the offence.
Action of blacklisting is 'civil death' for the party/entity and needs to be tested on the principles of natural justice, fair play in action and on the doctrine of proportionality.
12. In Kulja Industries Limited Vs. Chief General Manager, Western Telecom Project Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited and others (2014) 14 SCC 731, while referring to the passage from the decision in Mahabir Auto Stores Vs. Indian Oil Corporation (1990) 3 SCC 752, the Supreme Court has held :-

3 "20.
It is also well settled that even though the right of the writ petitioner is in the nature of a contractual right, the manner, the method and the motive behind the decision of the authority whether or not to enter into a contract is subject to judicial review on the touchstone of fairness, relevance, natural justice, non-discrimination,
equality and proportionality.
All these considerations that go to determine whether the action is sustainable in law have been sanctified by judicial pronouncements of this Court and are of seminal importance in a system that is committed to the rule of law.

Post Graduate Institute of Medical Education and Research and another 2020 Online SC 638 and Vet India Pharmaceuticals Ltd. Vs. State of U.P. and another (2021) 1 SCC 804.

Blacklisting is thus an extreme recourse for disciplining such supplier/contractor, who have intentionally committed breach of conditions/regulations under the contract or committed acts of omission and commission or fraud including falsification of record, misrepresentation.
However,
the period of black listing would depend upon the nature of offence committed by the erring contractor/supplier.
21. The Corporation is an instrumentality of State and expected to act and deal in a fair manner.
Its activities has a public element and therefore, there should be fairness and equality.
In the present case, no case of misappropriation or fraud is made out nor any loss has been caused to the Corporation, under the circumstances, the order of recovery and blacklisting cannot be sustained.
23. In the present case, even if one assumes that the petitioner has used other vehicles for transportation of food grains without seeking prior permission of the Corporation or Collector and breached the clause 26 of the NIT.
The imposition of maximum penalty of 10 years for breach of clause 26 of NIT, which incidentally is not one of the disqualification under the clause 40 is harsh,
excessive and unwarranted.
There has to be due and fair application of mind by the authority competent to impose the penalty.
Merely because of the reason, that clause 40.2 empowers the Corporation to impose such a penalty, would not mean that maximum penalty can be imposed,
without considering the gravity of the offence.

17. In the instant case, while disposing of the W.P. No.25551/2018, this Court has directed the respondent authority to decide/consider the representation of petitioner dated 10.10.2018 in the light of order dated 23.03.2018 passed in R.P. However, the representation of the petitioner was dismissed vide order dated 13.02.2019.
The order further mentioned that petitioner has not produced any new facts before the concerned authority and therefore, affirmed the order dated 21.11.2016.
18.
It is evident from the order dated 23.03.2018 passed in R.P. No.1277/2017 that the Ministry of Home Affairs summed the report from the Collector/District Magistrate, Jabalpur and also from the District Manager of the Corporation in regard to the illegalities committed by the petitioner,
wherein the statements of shop owners of concerned fair price shops were recorded by the authorities, who verified that food grains were duly supplied to them.
The Review Court after considering that these documents which notably were not denied by the respondent authorities, quashed the order of detention with liberty to the authority to pass appropriate orders after verification of the facts in the light of subsequent materials and evidence brought on record.

No. 1277/2017, no fresh action for detention was taken against the petitioner rather the District Manager of the Corporation vide letters dated 08.09.2017, 08.01.2018 and subsequently on 08.03.2021, urged the Managing Directer of the M/S Rameshwaram Transport vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 November, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57735395/
5 Corporation, District Vigilance Officer, Collector Office and District Supply Officer, Jabalpur and recommended withdrawal/cancellation of the order of blacklisting of petitioner.
As the order was made over six years ago, I am not inclined to remand the matter to the authorities.
Accordingly, the impugned order dated 13.02.2019 of respondent Corporation, is hereby quashed.
24. The petition is allowed.
